To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
parental styles of involvement have an effect on student performance, even after accounting the effect of context variables.
parental involvement styles have an influence on students' academic performance, and that the influence is greater in those schools with more distal or less controlling family profiles.

1) students whose parents exhibit a more distal profile of family involvement tend to demonstrate better results; 2) parental involvement styles have an individual and a school level effect on achievement, even after accounting the effect of context variables; 3) students whose parents present a more distal family profile tend to demonstrate better performance; and 4) schools with more communicative family involvement styles tend to demonstrate lower intra school differences.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the relationship between styles or profiles of parental involvement in the educational processes of students and their academic performance, and the influence that the school context exerts on this relationship.
the relationship between styles in parental involvement at home (control or communication) and academic performance.
the relationship between parental involvement and academic performance in Spanish secondary education.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

(a) parental involvement in schools is a positive factor for students' achievement, (b) the type of involvement is more important than the level of involvement, (c) the most beneficial type of involvement for student achievement is the one which is more communicative and less controlling, and (d) schools which have more communicatively oriented families tend to demonstrate lower intra-school differences in students' achievement.

a) parental involvement in education is a desirable phenomenon but it is not a panacea, b) the style of parental involvement is important, and c) the style of involvement in education should be considered in family information and training programs in schools.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
parental involvement is important for student academic success, and that the way parents choose to be involved is also important.
parental involvement is important, but it is not the only factor in the academic success or failure of students.
parental involvement styles are important predictors of students’ academic performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
parental involvement styles are related to students' academic performance, and that schools can influence this relationship.

parental involvement in the educational processes has a positive influence on students' academic performance, and that the most positive effects occur when parents exhibit a more communicative profile.
